title: Tabloid format, tabloid journalism, or the subject as source? — the Daily Mirror in Thomas Markle’s biography
context: Full section kept: 11 comments, 8 voices, 28 Oct – 4 Nov 2026. Mostly agreement and definition-polishing around two real disputes: what ‘tabloid’ picks out (paper format vs journalism genre), and whether the interviewee-as-source exception fits WP:BLPSOURCES as written. Heat is low — the timeline sits mostly on the floor, which is the correct result for this thread.

weak_points.note: The ban is stated without a single case: ‘or really for anything’ universalizes from no exhibit — and when challenged, the category does the work instead of evidence.

The retreat from tabloid (format) to tabloid journalism (genre) is never operationalized — no criterion decides which outlets count, which is exactly what Cortador later says blocks any guideline amendment.
The evidence question is never answered — nobody supplies a reliability record for the Mirror either way; the thread ends on the definitional point.
Reconstructed from the quoted guideline: the reading that ‘only available sources’ covers an interviewee-sourced allegation is a judgment call, and the amendment question turns on it.
The ‘pattern of negative stories’ inference is an abductive step stated in one breath — it would not survive BLP-weight scrutiny, but nobody presses it here.
Own-reading doubt: ‘attributed quote seems fine’ may be a judgment about this sentence rather than a general rule; the thread never separates the two.
